blocks.text: Ladner Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: streets and boundaries

items.t: Delta's 2024 annual report calls Ladner the hub of Delta's agriculture industry.
No court registry sits in Delta. The Province's courthouse directory lists Supreme Court registries at New Westminster, 651 Carnarvon Street, and Vancouver, 800 Smithe Street.

blocks.text: Ladner Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: the housing stock

items.t: The stock spans village houses, strata homes and farm parcels. A Commission report for Westham Island records 32.7 hectares, all Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) area.

blocks.text: Ladner Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The redemption period is six months unless the court orders otherwise, and the court may extend it before an order absolute, under the same Act.
Flood rules follow an as-is purchase: Delta records a permit area protecting development from flood hazards in Ladner East Rural (LV5).

blocks.text: Ladner Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Delta is protected by 67 kilometres of dikes and seawall, per its 2024 annual report.
Work impacting a dike needs approval from the Inspector of Dikes, per Delta's engineering criteria update.
A December 2022 king tide caused seepage, not a breach, beside Ladner Slough.

blocks.text: Ladner Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: development and new projects

items.t: The Chisholm Street Wharf in Ladner Village is under construction, with completion anticipated by late spring 2026, per Delta's February 24, 2026 news release.

items.t: Delta is a listed Speculation and Vacancy Tax area.

items.t: Check the flood covenant on title; Delta records an executed flood-proofing covenant on a Ladner-area subdivision.
Confirm parcel zoning with the City, not the listing, per Delta's zoning page.

faq.q: Which court handles a Ladner foreclosure?
faq.a: The British Columbia Supreme Court, by petition. The Law and Equity Act ties venue to the land's municipality or judicial district, treating Vancouver and New Westminster as one registry.

faq.q: How long can the owner still redeem?
faq.a: Six months, unless the court orders shorter or longer. The Law and Equity Act sets that default and allows an extension before an order absolute.

faq.q: Is Goods and Services Tax (GST) charged on a court-ordered sale?
faq.a: It depends on the property and parties. The Canada Revenue Agency treats a creditor's seizure of real property as a deemed sale by the debtor, with a possible rebate for a non-registrant seller. Confirm the tax status in writing before completion, and ask who collects or remits any tax payable on the particular sale being approved.

faq.q: Does buying "as is" change the flood checks?
faq.a: No, they matter more. Delta records flood-proofing covenants on Ladner-area lots and a flood-hazard permit area in Ladner East Rural. A court sale does not waive a covenant already registered on title, so the covenant wording should be read before any offer is written.
